# Real OpenPrintTag fixtures

Raw NFC-V memory dumps taken from Prusa's own spec repo,
[OpenPrintTag/openprinttag-specification](https://github.com/OpenPrintTag/openprinttag-specification)
(MIT licensed), not generated by this project's own encoder. Unlike the synthetic dumps
built in `tests/test_openprinttag_codec.py` and `tests_integration/tests/_openprinttag_fixtures.py`,
these exercise the wire format real tags actually use: a long-form NDEF record (payload >
255 bytes) and the 3-byte TLV length form, neither of which this project's own synthetic
builders produce.

- `prusa_sample_tag.bin` — `docs_src/sample_data/sample_tag.bin` from that repo.
- `prusa_test01_data.bin` — `tests/encode_decode/01_data.bin` from that repo. Its
  companion `01_info.yaml`/`01_input.yaml` are the ground truth the matching unit tests
  assert against (declared `tag_uid: E0040108662F6FBC`, expected field values, and
  spec-derived UUIDs from that repo's `utils/opt_check.py`).

The interoperability contract is pinned to official source commit
[`060e420892d66c062c8af440c97701aab96bac79`](https://github.com/OpenPrintTag/openprinttag-specification/tree/060e420892d66c062c8af440c97701aab96bac79);
the format has no on-wire version field. In `prusa_test01_data.bin`, offsets 35..37
are the final MIME record header `52 1c f5`, offsets 38..65 are the MIME type,
and offsets 66..310 are its 245-byte CBOR payload. Tests extract these fixed offsets
independently of Spoolman's NDEF parser to verify the mobile payload-only transport.

The pinned official `utils/rec_info.py --show-data --opt-check --tag-uid E0040108662F6FBC`
also validates `prusa_test01_data.bin`: both `validate.errors` and `opt_check.errors` are
empty, and its derived instance UUID is `bf63e92d-9ca5-53d7-9fab-ffdd0240c585`.
Only the recommended `nominal_full_length` and `actual_full_length` fields are absent.

## Swift writer interoperability fixture

`printfarmer_swift_pla.json` contains the exact bytes supplied by PrintFarmer's Swift
`NFCTagParser.createOpenPrintTagPayload` and its golden-byte XCTest, not bytes generated
by Spoolman's tests. The corrected base64 is asserted against the supplied hex.
The MIME payload has an empty meta map and main fields
`{8: 0, 9: 0, 10: "PLA", 17: 1000.0, 18: 200.0, 19: h'FF0000'}`.

`test_actual_swift_writer_payload_through_codec_and_scan` exercises those bytes through
Spoolman's actual codec and HTTP routes, including read-only enrichment, explicit creation,
database reopen, repeated creation requests and conflicting enrichment of an existing link.
Actual full weight becomes the spool's initial weight; nominal filament weight is absent.
The decoded color is `ff0000`, while the persisted filament's standard color normalization
returns `FF0000`.

The pinned official reference reader also accepts these exact bytes with
`rec_info.py --unhex --config-file data/config_noroot.yaml --show-data --opt-check --tag-uid E0040108662F6FBC`:
both validation/error lists are empty and the derived instance UUID matches the fixture.
It warns about absent recommended fields, absent optional aux region, and underivable
brand/material/package UUIDs. These are software fixtures, not a physical NFC capture.
